title: "7.9 Gate record"
order: 9

::: {.callout-important}
## The gates

**Top-decile capture ≥ {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}}** of deteriorations — a lift of at
least {{< var ews.gate.lift_min >}}× — and **PR-AUC above the base rate**, both on the held-out
{{< var ews.test_share >}} of the booked book ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-split)). Current values
{{< var ews.capture >}} and {{< var ews.pr_auc >}} against a base rate of
{{< var ews.base_rate >}}: **both met**, capture narrowly (finding 3). **AUC is reported, not
gated**: {{< var ews.auc >}}, held to a sanity floor of {{< var ews.gate.auc_floor >}} only, so
that a near-random model cannot pass on capture alone. The gates are on the model's ranking;
no gate covers the tiers or the triggers.
:::

## Why the gate is on capture, with AUC reported {#ews-why-capture}

This is a deliberate design, recorded in the code itself:

```python
# Gate (Option B — honest gate for the noise-capped synthetic deterioration target).   # ews/src/train.py
# The DGP label carries a large logit-noise + Bernoulli draw, so the oracle ceiling is
# ~0.70 AUC; we gate on what the data genuinely supports and report AUC for transparency.
CAPTURE_GATE = 0.20  # >= 20% of deteriorations in the top decile == 2x lift
AUC_REPORT_FLOOR = 0.60  # sanity floor only (model must beat near-random); not the headline gate
```

Two reasons, both measured in [7.5](performance.qmd#ews-ceiling):

- **The data caps AUC, for every model.** The label is drawn with noise twice over
  ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-label)). On the held-out accounts the generator's own noise-free logit
  reaches {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}}, and the strongest model on every observable
  column {{< var ceiling.ews.oracle_model.auc >}}; the committed model, {{< var ews.auc >}}, is a
  hair below the second. An AUC gate set where the origination models' is would be failed by
  every honest model, and the only way to "pass" it would be to lower it until something did —
  which this platform never does (invariant: gates are never relaxed, [D9](../d9-implementation.qmd#gates-are-hard-asserts-recomputed-independently)).
- **Capture is what the use needs.** A review team works the top of the list. The question
  that decides whether the model is useful is how much of the coming trouble sits in the
  accounts it can call, not how well the model orders the quiet accounts at the bottom.

AUC stays on every page, reported beside its ceiling, so no reader has to take its absence
from the gate on trust. The comment's "~0.70" is the noise-free logit over the whole book,
{{< var ceiling.ews.latent_book >}}; on the held-out accounts the comparable figure is
{{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} — compare within a sample ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-ceiling)).

## Where they are asserted

At the end of training, in `ews/src/train.py`, after the model, `metadata.json`, the panel
cache and the validation report have been written:

```python
assert capture >= CAPTURE_GATE, f"GATE FAIL: capture {capture:.3f} < {CAPTURE_GATE} (2x)"
assert pr_auc > base, f"GATE FAIL: PR-AUC {pr_auc:.4f} <= base rate {base:.4f}"
assert auc >= AUC_REPORT_FLOOR, f"GATE FAIL: AUC {auc:.4f} < sanity floor {AUC_REPORT_FLOOR}"
```

`capture`, `pr_auc` and `auc` are computed on the held-out accounts' probabilities, capture by
`top_decile_capture`; `base` is the deterioration rate over the whole booked book
({{< var ews.base_rate >}}, the same to the printed precision as the held-out
{{< var ews.base_rate_holdout >}}, because the split is stratified). The asserts are the
script's last step, so a model that misses a gate still leaves its artifacts behind; the run
fails, and `verify.py` then fails on those artifacts (below). The gate values are also written
into `ews/models/metadata.json`, under `["gate"]["capture_min"]`, `["gate"]["pr_auc_min"]`
(the string `"base_rate"`) and `["gate"]["auc_report_floor"]`.

## Where they are recomputed, independently

`verify.py` carries its own copies:

```python
EWS_CAPTURE_GATE = 0.20      # top-decile capture >= 20% of deteriorations = 2x lift   # verify.py
EWS_AUC_FLOOR = 0.60         # sanity floor only, not the headline gate
```

Its check, `check_ews`, reads no stored metric. It:

1. fails at once, naming them, if `ews_model.pkl`, `metadata.json` or `panel_features.parquet`
   is missing;
2. loads `ews_model.pkl`, builds the features from the committed portfolio with
   `compute_ews_features` — which recomputes the score through `predict_score_pd` and reads
   the committed panel cache — and redraws the held-out split with the platform seed and
   stratification;
3. recomputes AUC with `roc_auc_score`, PR-AUC with `average_precision_score`, and capture
   **with its own code**, not by importing `top_decile_capture`:

   ```python
   k = max(1, int(round(0.10 * len(y_te))))                       # verify.py
   capture = float(y_te[np.argsort(p)[::-1][:k]].sum() / y_te.sum())
   base = float(y.mean())
   ```

4. fails if capture is below its own constant, if PR-AUC is at or below the base rate, or if
   AUC is below the floor — and on success prints AUC as "reported, not gated".

It does not read the tier cutoffs, re-tier the book or run the triggers: they are outside the
gate. On `main`, `verify.py` then recomputes every fact in this chapter — the gate figures,
their bootstrap intervals and margin, the tiers, every trigger clause, the watchlist — and
fails, naming the key, if any page would print a stale value ([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)).

This is why **a relaxed local gate cannot pass.** Lowering `CAPTURE_GATE` in `train.py` lets a
weaker model finish training, but `verify.py` recomputes that model's capture against the
constant it carries itself, and fails. The panel cache cannot be edited around the gate either:
the model's predictions move with it, and the recomputed gate moves with them.

## The what-if equals the batch {#ews-whatif}

Not a gate, but a control on what the workbench shows. The v2 EWS what-if re-tiers the book
with `risk_tier` and re-flags it with `flag_triggers` under a reviewer's values; with the
committed values it must reproduce the batch exactly ([7.1](purpose.qmd#who-consumes-it-and-how)):

- **`tests/test_app_v2.py`**: an empty body reproduces each sampled account's batch tier and
  triggers, and the book's tier counts in `/api/ews/summary`; an out-of-range value or an
  inverted tier band is refused.
- **`tests/test_app_v2_ui_bodies.py`**: what the browser actually sends on every drag — both
  cutoffs and every trigger threshold, explicitly — re-tiers all {{< var ews.n_book >}} accounts
  to their batch tier and reproduces the batch triggers on a sample. Tiers are re-derived from
  the unrounded probability, never from the rounded `prob` column.
- **The facts**: the tiers, triggers, probabilities and watchlist the facts compute equal
  `score_population`'s, account by account (`tests/test_wiki_ews_facts.py`).

`verify.py`'s own v2 smoke check asserts the what-if for adjudication, not for Early Warning;
the EWS what-if is covered by the tests above. If any fails, the workbench is showing a tier
the batch does not: fix the drift, never the test.

## What the gates do not cover

- **The tiers.** The cutoffs are written by the same run, from in-sample quantiles, and no
  check compares the mix they give on held-out accounts with the mix intended (finding 1).
- **The whole-book figures.** Every gate figure is held out; nothing stops a whole-book figure
  being quoted (finding 2).
- **Calibration.** All three measures are about ranking; the Low tier's under-prediction
  passes them (finding 5).
- **The triggers.** No gate measures them; one clause cannot fire and the rest barely beat the
  base rate (findings 6 and 7).
- **The score.** Passing the gate does not show the model ranks better than `pd_score` alone
  (finding 4).

## History

| Version | Change | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| development, before `stage-4` | the design brief's gate (an AUC minimum and a higher capture) found unreachable on this data and replaced, before the module was first committed (`ews/docs/enhancement_notes.md`) | not committed |
| `stage-4` (commit `dbca721`) | gates introduced with the Early Warning model, in `train.py` and `verify.py` | capture {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}}, PR-AUC above the base rate, AUC floor {{< var ews.gate.auc_floor >}} |
| `stage-5`, `v1.0` to `v1.5`, `main` | unchanged | as above |

The gates have not changed since they were committed, and they are never relaxed to let a
model pass ([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd#gates-are-hard-asserts-recomputed-independently)).
The pre-commit change is recorded because it was made with the model's result in view, which is
part of why finding 3 matters. The brief's stronger gate is not unreachable for want of a
better model: on the held-out accounts not even the generator's noise-free logit meets it
([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-finding-3)). A change to any gate would be a change of the committed
promise: made on `main`, recorded in a new version tag, and shown in this table.
